newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO, ING shares up on hidden reserves report.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO, ING shares up on hidden reserves report.

text.p: ABN AMRO and ING Group shares rose in response to a report on Dutch banks' hidden reserves by stockbroker ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, dealers and analysts said.
The report estimated the positive effect on earnings and dividends of the unveiling of hidden reserves, which will be made with their 1996 results in coming months.
ABN AMRO shares jumped to a year's high of 119.50 guilders before easing back to 118.50 at 1030 GMT, up 2.20 percent from the previous close.
At the same time, ING shares stood at a year's peak of 66.70, 1.40 guilders or 2.1 percent stronger.
Banking is the only sector in the Netherlands which is allowed to create hidden reserves and provisions to cover possible loan losses.
The size of the so-called provision for general risks (VAR) has been known only to the banks themselves and the Dutch central bank until now.
But, ahead of the introduction of European guidelines in 1998, Dutch banks have decided to collectively reveal the size of these reserves early.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, a unit of ABN AMRO, said the change meant total risk provisioning would fall, boosting earnings.
It said ING's earnings per share and dividends would be between five and eight percent higher in 1997 than its current estimates of 4.65 and 2.00 guilders respectively, .
Analysts Margot van der Velden and Bryan Crossley estimated ING's VAR at 2.8 billion guilders.
They said market estimates of ABN AMRO's VAR ranged between 3.0 billion and 4.0 billion guilders.
Other analysts said they agreed with these estimates but pointed out that the existence of the reserves was not new.
IRIS analyst Bart van der Feen said Dutch investors had already factored the effects into their forecasts.
"Perhaps for foreign investors it may be a surprise," he added.
Most analysts said they were positive on ABN AMRO's prospects.
One analyst said another reason for its share price strength may be that the bank was recently selected as one of the favourite shares for the first half of 1997 by brokers contacted by Reuters.
"It remains my favourite," said Ton Gietman, banking analyst with HSBC Van Meer James Capel.
